newsitem.title: USA: Bank bill to go to Commerce Committee, Lazio says.
newsitem.headline: Bank bill to go to Commerce Committee, Lazio says.

text.p: In a move that could delay the passage of bank reform, the Republican House leadership has decided to allow the Commerce Committee to review legislative proposals produced by the Banking Committee, a member of the leadership said on Wednesday.

After the Banking Committee produces a bill, "it will go to the Commerce Committee to look at the piece that affects securities and insurance," Rep. Rick Lazio, Deputy Majority Whip, told a meeting of the New York Bankers Association here.
Commerce Committee chair Thomas Bliley "would like to have his viewpoint expressed," Lazio said.
But Lazio, Republican of New York, said it had not been decided if the Commerce Committee would hold a full-blown mark-up of the bank reform measure with committee members free to offer amendments.

Whether the two committees can collaborate is "uncertain," he said. But if both committees held separate sessions to amend the bill, that would give opponents of bank reform "two bites at the apple," he said.
In the last Congress, only the Banking Committee considered bank reform measures.
But a comprehensive bill to overhaul the financial sector failed and Congress passed only a limited measure to shore up the federal insurance fund for savings institutions.

Lazio said the Republican leadership also planned to establish a special task force on bank reform issues. The task force would not write legislation but would be "for dealing in one place to help vet some of the tactical and strategic problems in bringing this to the House floor," he said.
The Republican task force would likely include Commerce chair Bliley of Virginia and securities subcommittee chair Michael Oxley of Ohio, Lazio said.
The task force would also include Banking Committee chair Jim Leach of Iowa, a few other members of the banking committee and some members of the leadership, Lazio said.
Lazio is the only member of Congress to sit on both the Banking and Commerce Committees.
House Speaker Newt Gingrich hopes to get a bank reform measure voted on by the full house within six months, Lazio told the banking group.
